rawFindings.title: Removing unicode line terminators from valid escapes set breaks string escape detection
rawFindings.explanation: The original VALID_STRING_ESCAPES set included the Unicode line separator (\u2028) and paragraph separator (\u2029) characters, which are valid escape sequences in JavaScript strings. The change removed these characters from the set, which means the rule may incorrectly report them as unnecessary escapes, leading to false positives or even incorrect linting errors for valid code containing these escapes.
rawFindings.suggestion:
Restore the inclusion of \u2028 and \u2029 back into the VALID_STRING_ESCAPES set as follows:

const VALID_STRING_ESCAPES = new Set("\\nrvtbfux\n\r\u2028\u2029");

rawFindings.title: Incorrect VALID_STRING_ESCAPES set omits valid escaped Unicode line separator U+2028 and paragraph separator U+2029
rawFindings.explanation: The change removes \u2028 and \u2029 characters from the VALID_STRING_ESCAPES set (line 27). These Unicode characters are valid escape sequences recognized in JavaScript string literals and should not be flagged as useless. Removing them causes the rule to incorrectly report legitimate escapes as unnecessary.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore \u2028 and \u2029 in the VALID_STRING_ESCAPES set to avoid false positives, reverting line 27 to: const VALID_STRING_ESCAPES = new Set("\\nrvtbfux\n\r\u2028\u2029");

rawFindings.explanation: The change removes the Unicode line and paragraph separator characters (\u2028 and \u2029) from the set of valid string escapes. These characters are valid escape sequences for strings and omitting them may cause valid escapes to be flagged as unnecessary mistakenly.
